A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LinkAlign framework and AmbiDB dataset. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v3 reports original schema-linking and SQL-generation experiments, runtime measurements, ablations and a 500-example Spider error analysis.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds GPT-4 evaluations and an end-to-end efficiency experiment in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The three stages, agent roles and single-database adaptations remain the same. However, Section 3.3 removes 'through pseudo-SQL generation' from the Database Expert's validation description. The PDFs do not establish whether this procedure changed or its description merely became less specific.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same schema-linking and SQL-generation tasks using Spider, BIRD, AmbiDB and Spider 2.0-Lite, including the same single- and multi-database scenarios. The new efficiency study samples an already used benchmark.

E2.justification: New Table 8 compares LinkAlign's end-to-end efficiency against CHESS, RSL-SQL and DIN-SQL; v3's runtime comparison covered only LinkAlign variants. Baseline membership in the existing accuracy comparisons is unchanged. The added GPT-4 rows are LinkAlign configurations.

E3.justification: Tables 4–5 add GPT-4 configurations for the existing simplified LinkAlign evaluations. Appendix G introduces a separate protocol using 50 randomly sampled Spider 2.0-Lite examples and DeepSeek-V3 to measure end-to-end time and token consumption. Existing evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds an analysis of whole-pipeline runtime and token costs relative to competing methods, extending v3's per-stage timing analysis. The component ablations, error analysis and associated figures remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. Table 8 adds averages without uncertainty estimates, consistent with the existing timing-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 4–5 add LinkAlign with GPT-4 EX scores of 91.2% on Spider-dev and 61.6% on Bird-dev. These are additional configurations, not improvements to existing runs. Table 8 adds five methods' time/token results, including Pipeline at 127.6 seconds and 8507.4 tokens. Previously reported numerical results and plotted findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The schema definitions, Equations 1–4 and metric definitions retain the same mathematical content. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: the three-stage LinkAlign framework, AmbiDB and improved schema linking and SQL generation. The headline Spider 2.0-Lite result and claim remain 33.09% using open-source LLMs.

C2.justification: Appendix G newly interprets end-to-end measurements as showing limited overhead and attributes Pipeline efficiency to avoiding full-schema processing. This interpretation needs qualification because Agent costs exceed DIN-SQL's. Existing mechanism explanations and limitations remain substantively unchanged; the limitations move to Appendix H.

D1.justification: Appendix G specifies the new efficiency study's sample size and backbone. Conversely, Section 3.3 removes the explicit pseudo-SQL validation detail. Existing embedding and retrieval parameters, AmbiDB construction instructions and code-access disclosure are retained; the new GPT-4 results receive little additional implementation documentation.

R1.justification: v4 adds a Pei et al. citation for reasoning techniques and expands Appendix A with Solid-SQL, TA-SQL and model-compression literature. These additions broaden discussion of robustness, hallucination mitigation and possible cost-reduction approaches without redefining the paper's central positioning.

P1.justification: v4 updates authors and affiliations, adds acknowledgments, corrects headings and makes localized wording edits. It adds Appendix G and moves the existing limitations section to Appendix H. Most prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 8, expands Tables 4–5 with GPT-4 rows, and moves and resizes Table 7 from a display spanning both columns to one column. Other content reflows, while all four figures retain identical graphics.

improvement.justification: The GPT-4 rows make the existing GPT-4 baseline comparisons more informative, and Appendix G adds practical end-to-end cost evidence beyond v3's per-stage timings. These modestly strengthen evaluation. The gain is limited by sparse setup details and an overbroad low-overhead interpretation: Table 8 reports Agent at 183.5 seconds and 12486.5 tokens versus DIN-SQL at 146.3 seconds and 8600.0 tokens.
